title: Interactive Timeline
thesis: The visitor flies in one continuous zoom from deep time to a single week of the story, watches Earth, Terra and Kha-Ren run in step and then diverge at each artifact discovery, compares any moment across the three in their own calendars, reads the physics behind each event tagged from established to fiction with real citations, and asks questions answered only from the published event data, never past the reading point they chose.

axes.name: Multi-calendar chronology
axes.metric: What the date engine computes, checked against CODEX/CHRONOLOGY: calendars converted by the CALENDAR_SYSTEMS formulas (A.T. = CE + 3537; CE = Cycle x 75 + Year - 4750), rows of the CALENDAR_SYSTEMS and MASTER_TIMELINE tables that the engine reproduces or lists as canon discrepancies, and the share of event positions computed rather than typed. A rater runs the repo's conversion tests, or converts 5 rows of the CROSS-CALENDAR REFERENCE TABLE on the page and compares them with the formulas.
ladder: Absent: no date model exists; nothing places an event in time.
Events carry a hand-typed date label only; their order on the page comes from list order, not from a number.
Every event has a numeric Earth-CE year (negative for BCE, years-ago values for deep time) and its on-screen position is computed from that number.

One scale function (piecewise linear with stated breakpoints, or log of years before the story present with the present handled explicitly) maps every shipped event, from the oldest to 2068 CE, inside the axis at the widest view with 0 clipped, and ticks are labelled Gyr ago, BCE or CE by range; when the oldest event at or below the spoiler ceiling is younger than 1 Gyr, the deep range is carried by cited [ESTABLISHED] anchors (the age of the Earth, the age of the universe).

Terra's A.T. date is computed by the CALENDAR_SYSTEMS formula A.T. = CE + 3537 (BCE n read as CE -n, as the table does), reproducing every Terra cell of the CROSS-CALENDAR REFERENCE TABLE (2068 CE = 5605 A.T., 1 CE = 3538 A.T.); every Terra event at or after 0 A.T. shows its A.T. date beside CE, events before 0 A.T. show 'pre-A.T.' as canon states, never a negative A.T. year, and the ~400-day year is used only for ages (rung 7).

Kha-Ren's Cycle.Year is computed by the CALENDAR_SYSTEMS formula CE = Cycle x 75 + Year - 4750, with Year from 0 to 74 (Cycle 90, Year 68 = 2068 CE; C1.Y0 = 4675 BCE); events before C1.Y0 show 'pre-calendar' as the CALENDAR_SYSTEMS table does, and every event after both epochs shows all three dates, each produced by code, none typed.

Date uncertainty modelled: every approximate CODEX date (a '~' or a range) is stored as an interval whose width follows a rule written in the data file (for example +/-1% of years before the story present for '~', the stated endpoints for a range), drawn as a span, and carried through every conversion.

Age convention: a function converts a biological Earth-standard age to native-calendar years by the CALENDAR_SYSTEMS rule (x 365/400 for Terra, x 1 for Earth and Kha-Ren), reproducing all 8 rows of the AGE EQUIVALENCE CONVENTION table within 0.2 year (the two Terra rows: 42 gives 38.3 against ~38.3, 67 gives 61.1 against ~61.3); elapsed spans between two dates are the differences of their native date numbers, the rule cross-dimension-compare rung 6 uses, and the page states that canon converts dates by offset and ages by year length.

Conversion tests in the repo check at least 20 dated rows from CALENDAR_SYSTEMS and MASTER_TIMELINE, including every row of the CROSS-CALENDAR REFERENCE TABLE; each row either matches within the interval rung 6 gives it or sits in a canon-discrepancy list in the repo that shows both values and the reading the engine follows (the list includes ~3537 BCE: table C15.Y~13 against formula C16.Y13, and 2065 CE: MASTER_TIMELINE C90.Y~15 against formula C90.Y65); the test fails on any row that neither matches nor is listed, so 0 mismatches are unlisted.

Relative dates solved: events dated only by order or by chapter span (before X, during Y, chapters 9 to 11) are placed by a constraint solver over Allen's 13 interval relations (James F. Allen, Communications of the ACM, 1983) with propagation by Allen's transitivity table; a test feeds it an inconsistent set and it reports the conflict, and the page shows the constraints behind any placed event.

Reference standard: the calendar-conversion rigour of Reingold and Dershowitz, Calendrical Calculations (Cambridge University Press): every displayed date, native conversion and uncertainty band is derived by the engine from CODEX-sourced constraints with 0 hand-placed positions; a test regenerates all positions and diffs them against the shipped data with 0 changes, and every unsatisfiable constraint is reported with both source lines.

G0.evidence: no page exists: the hub lists 'timeline' as planned in labs/assets/js/config/site.config.js, and no module computes TRIVERSE dates or calendars. The site's only chronology code, labs/assets/js/altverse/render/chronology.js (48 lines, fmtYear formats Gyr/Myr/kyr), serves Altverse and is not part of this lab; the unported prototype TRIVERSE_TIMELINE.html in the TRIVERSE repo is not on the site and does not count.

axes.name: Divergence structure
axes.metric: How faithfully the timeline's structure encodes the saga's dimension cosmology: count of structural features present (dimension field, typed discovery events with stored offsets, divergence drawn from data, typed cross-dimension links, structural and core layers, character threads, a sourced era list, causal edges), read from the event schema and checked on the page against CODEX DIVERGENCE_POINTS and MASTER_TIMELINE.
ladder: Absent: no events, so no structure; nothing records which dimension an event belongs to.
A single flat list of events with no dimension field.
Every event carries a dimension field whose value is one of the six canon dimensions (three expression, two structural, one core), and the page shows it.

Each expression dimension's artifact discovery is a typed event (Kha-Ren ~8000 BCE, Terra ~3537 BCE, Earth at the date a rulings file in the repo names, with its reason, among canon's 1944 detection, 2031 access and 2068 table date), and every event in an expression lane stores its signed offset in years from its own lane's discovery.

Divergence drawn to canon from data: before a lane's discovery its development-stage label matches the lanes not yet diverged (Neolithic at ~8000 BCE for Earth and Terra, Bronze Age at ~3537 BCE for Earth and Terra, per MASTER_TIMELINE and DIVERGENCE_POINTS); at its discovery event the lane shows a divergence marker and from then on its DIVERGENCE_POINTS response label (containment, acceleration, discovery); editing a discovery date in the data file moves its marker; Earth's marker shows the ruled date and lists canon's other two; the lanes are never drawn as one line that forks (DIVERGENCE_POINTS: 'not parallel timelines', 'separate branes').

Typed cross-dimension links: every canon contact or crossing between dimensions at or below the spoiler ceiling is stored as an edge with a type and drawn as a connector between lanes at the moment it occurs.

The two structural dimensions and the core dimension render as layers beneath or between the expression lanes, not as three more parallel lanes; each layer carries the events the spoiler ceiling admits, and a layer whose events are all above the ceiling shows as a named, empty layer.

Character threads: at least 6 named characters have lifelines in the data (first appearance, key events, last state at or below the spoiler ceiling) drawn as threads inside their lanes and crossing lanes where canon moves them.

Eras: an era list file in the repo names every era with its CODEX source line (at least Terra's Early Artifact Era 0-1000 A.T., Great Unification 1000-2000 A.T. and Unified civilization, and Kha-Ren's span from discovery to caste formalization, ~8000 to ~4675 BCE, and its caste era from C1.Y0), each with a start and end interval from the chronology engine; the page shows each lane's era at the cursor, or 'no named era' where canon names none.
Causal edges: events carry typed cause links (caused, enabled, responded to) within and across lanes, each with its CODEX source, and selecting an event highlights its causes and its consequences.

Structure complete against canon: a script checks that every dimension, era, discovery point, cross-dimension link and named character in CODEX/CHRONOLOGY appears in the graph or in a documented exclusion list with a reason (spoiler, scaffold), with 0 unexplained gaps.

G0.evidence: no page exists: there is no event data or schema on the site, so no dimension field, discovery event, lane, link or thread exists.

axes.name: Deep-time zoom
axes.metric: Zoom range and legibility of the drawn timeline: view width at the widest and narrowest zoom in years, overlapping labels counted at 5 named views (the whole chronology, 8000 BCE to 2068 CE, 1868 to 2068 CE, the year 2068, and a 2-week window at the story's 'Weeks 1-2' row), levels of detail, and the number of linked views kept in sync. A rater zooms the page end to end at 1440 px and reads the axis and labels at each named view.
ladder: Absent: nothing is drawn.
A static image or a plain list of events; no drawn time axis.
One drawn time axis (SVG or canvas) with event marks at their dates; no zoom.
The three expression lanes are drawn on the shared axis with event marks and labels; at the default view at 1440 px, 0 labels overlap and no label text is smaller than 11 px.
Zoom and pan by wheel, drag and pinch, anchored on the pointer, over at least 6 orders of magnitude of view width, with tick labels recomputed at every zoom level.

The full range: view width runs continuously from at least 1 Gyr (the whole chronology) down to 1 week, about 11 orders of magnitude, with 0 overlapping labels at these 5 views: the whole chronology, 8000 BCE to 2068 CE, 1868 to 2068 CE, the year 2068, and a 2-week window at the story's 'Weeks 1-2' row.
Semantic zoom with at least 3 levels of detail (eras, events, chapter-scale beats); marks closer than 8 px merge into a counted cluster that splits as the visitor zooms in.

Flights between distant moments (deep time to the story present) animate as a combined zoom-out, pan and zoom-in path in the manner of van Wijk and Nuij (IEEE InfoVis 2003, smooth and efficient zooming and panning), in at most 1.5 s.
Linked views: an overview strip of the whole chronology with a brush marking the current window, the main timeline and the event detail panel stay in sync within one animation frame.

Storyline layout: character threads are laid out by crossing minimisation (as in Tanahashi and Ma, IEEE TVCG 2012, or StoryFlow, Liu et al., IEEE TVCG 2013), and the page reports the crossing count of the current layout beside the count for the same threads in data order, the first lower than the second.

Reference standard ChronoZoom (UC Berkeley and Microsoft Research, 2012) for zoom continuity, joined to diverging lanes and storyline threads in one view: a rater zooms from the oldest event down to a 1-week window, the finest dating canon gives (MASTER_TIMELINE's week-level 2068 rows), in one gesture sequence with no reload, no blank frame and 0 label overlaps.

G0.evidence: no page exists: nothing draws this lab. The only timeline renderer on the site, labs/assets/js/altverse/render/chronology.js (48 lines), draws Altverse era bands as a DOM list with no zoom or lanes, and is not part of this lab.

axes.metric: What the visitor learns by comparing moments across Earth, Terra and Kha-Ren: the comparison features present and their correctness.
